Lesson Objectives 
 
By the end of the lesson, students will be able to: 
 1. Use vocabulary related to presents (toy, book, bike, watch, phone, flowers, clothes). 
 2. Ask and answer: “What is your favourite present?” – “My favourite present is a …” 
 3. Express likes/dislikes with presents: “I like… / I don’t like…” 
 4. Write short sentences about their favourite gift. 
 
Teaching Instruments 
 • Flashcards/pictures of common presents 👉 
 • Realia (toy gift box, ribbon, small objects) 
 • Whiteboard / projector 
 • Worksheets (matching, gap-fill, sentence building) 
 • Ball or soft toy for games 
 
Lesson Structure 
 
1. Warm-up (10 min) 
 • Teacher shows a gift box 👉 and asks: “What is this?” (Gift/Present).

• Ask: “Do you like presents?” → students answer Yes! 
 • Quick brainstorm: “What presents do people get on birthdays?” → elicit vocabulary. 
 
2. Presentation (15 min) 
 • Introduce key vocabulary with flashcards: toy, book, bike, watch, flowers, phone, clothes. 
 • Introduce question/answer: 
 • What is your favourite present? 
 • My favourite present is a book. 
 • Drill pronunciation and short dialogues. 
 
3. Practice (Controlled) (15 min) 
 • Matching exercise: Match words with pictures of presents. 
 • Gap-fill: 
192

1. My favourite present is a ___. 
 2. I like _. I don’t like _. 
 • Pair work: Students ask/answer: “What is your favourite present?” 
 
4. Production (20 min) 
 • Game 1: Pass the Present 👉 – Students pass a toy box while music plays. When music stops, 
the student opens it and answers: “My favourite present is…” 
 • Game 2: Present Survey – Students walk around asking 3 classmates: “What is your favourite 
present?” Then report: “Ali’s favourite present is a bike. Sara’s favourite present is flowers.” 
 • Game 3: Present Charades – One student mimes opening a present (bike, toy, phone), others 
guess. 
 
5. Writing Task (10 min) 
 • Students write 4–5 sentences about their favourite present. 
Example: “My favourite present is a watch. I got it for my birthday. It is black. I like it very 
much.” 
 
6. Wrap-up (5 min) 
 • Quick-fire questions: “What is your favourite present?” → go around the class. 
 • Teacher ends: “Presents make us happy!” 👉 
 
Teaching Methods 
 • PPP (Presentation–Practice–Production) 
 • Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) 
 • Role-play and pair work 
 • Game-based learning 
 
Types of Learning Activities 
 • Vocabulary drill 
 • Matching & gap-fill tasks 
 • Pair speaking practice 
 • Games (Pass the Present, Survey, Charades) 
 • Writing short sentences 
 
Assessment 
 • Observation during Q&A and games 
 • Accuracy in gap-fill and speaking tasks

• Written sentences checked for correct structure 
 • Exit ticket: Each student says one correct sentence (“My favourite present is a …”) 
 
Homework (Task) 
 • Write 5 sentences about the best present you have ever received. 
Example: “I got a bike for my birthday. It was red. I liked it very much. It was my favourite 
present.”

Lesson Objectives 
 
By the end of the lesson, students will be able to: 
 1. Understand and use basic conjunctions (and, but, so, because) in simple sentences. 
 2. Write short congratulation messages (e.g., birthday, exam success, wedding). 
 3. Connect sentences logically when writing. 
 4. Improve writing accuracy and creativity. 
 
Teaching Instruments 
 • Whiteboard/markers 
 • Flashcards with conjunctions 
 • Worksheets (fill-in-the-gap, sentence-building, writing prompts) 
 • Sample congratulation cards 👉 
 • Projector/PowerPoint (optional) 
 • Sticky notes, colored pens 
 
Lesson Structure 
 
1. Warm-up (10 min) 
 • Teacher shows a birthday card that says “Congrats!” 👉

• Ask: “When do we say Congrats?” (Birthday, exam, wedding, new baby). 
 • Brainstorm 2–3 situations on the board. 
 
2. Presentation (15 min) 
 • Introduce grammar: and, but, so, because with examples. 
 • I like pizza and pasta. 
 • I like tea, but I don’t like coffee. 
 • It was raining, so I stayed at home. 
 • I stayed at home because I was sick. 
 • Write on the board, drill with class. 
 
3. Practice (Controlled) (15 min) 
194

• Worksheet task 1: Fill in the blanks with correct conjunction. 
 • I like apples ___ I don’t like bananas. 
 • It’s my friend’s birthday, ___ I bought a gift. 
 • She is happy ___ she passed the exam. 
 • Pair work: Students join 2 short sentences with conjunctions. 
 
4. Writing Production (20 min) 
 • Teacher shows model congratulation messages: 
 • “Congrats on your birthday! I hope you are happy and healthy.” 
 • “Congrats! You studied hard, so you passed the exam.” 
 • Students write a short Congrats card (4–5 sentences) using at least 2 conjunctions. 
 • Peer check: Exchange cards and read each other’s messages. 
 
5. Fun Game (10 min) 
 • “Conjunction Chain” – Students sit in a circle. 
 • Student 1: “I like apples.” 
 • Student 2: “I like apples and I like bananas.” 
 • Student 3: “I like apples and I like bananas, but I don’t like oranges.” 
 • Continue around circle → fun, memory-based practice. 
 
6. Wrap-up (5 min) 
 • Quick-fire: Teacher says a sentence, students add correct conjunction. 
 • Example: “I like cats … (but) … I don’t like dogs.” 
 • Review: What did we learn today?

 • PPP (Presentation–Practice–Production) 
 • Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) 
 • Writing-based learning 
 • Game-based learning

 • Gap-fill exercises 
 • Sentence combining 
 • Pair work dialogues

• Writing congratulation cards 
 • Conjunction chain game 
 
Assessment 
 • Participation in grammar practice 
 • Correct use of conjunctions in sentences 
 • Quality of short writing task (Congrats message) 
 • Teacher observation during games and peer-check 
 
Homework (Task) 
 • Write two congratulation messages (5–6 sentences each) using and, but, so, because. 
Examples: 
 1. To a friend who got a new job. 
 2. To a cousin who graduated.
